prompt: Prime-time adult animated sitcom characters with simple rounded cartoon bodies, flat colour and black outlines, but every face is painted with startling real skin: pores, stubble, wrinkles, wet tired eyes, real eyelids, far more lifelike than anything around it, no feature exaggerated. Every colour is laid on in thick visible oil brushstrokes. Seen side-on as a cross-section like a lit stage with its near wall cut away: a secret 1930s basement speakeasy that is also a mint: rows of black iron printing presses with simple faces painted on their sides throw sheets of blank green paper money with no printing on it into the air like confetti; a band of gangsters in pinstripe suits plays trumpet, double bass and drums on a little stage; a tall skinny mayor in a bowler hat with a gold chain, a long narrow face, hollow cheeks and a pencil-thin grey moustache dances on a table. Emerald lamps hang over the presses, gold spotlights hit the stage, scarlet velvet curtains, a black-and-white tiled floor slick with spilled champagne. Along the top of the frame, a dark strip of the bakery above: its floor joists and floorboards cut through, flour dust sifting down through the cracks. Most of the frame is the basement's warm blaze against the dark; the brightest values are the gold stage spots and the flying green notes catching the emerald lamps. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
